summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, gastrostomy dependence, cervical spine hardware erosion, and chronic anemia, was admitted due to elevated creatinine and symptoms of dehydration, including fatigue, nausea, poor oral intake, and worsening diarrhea. He was found to have acute kidney injury likely due to volume depletion from increased diarrhea and reduced intake, with hyponatremia that resolved with IV hydration. A urinary tract infection caused by E. coli was identified and treated with antibiotics. He received two units of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia, which remained unexplained but consistent with chronic disease. A colonoscopy revealed normal mucosa, confirming that chronic diarrhea is likely due to anatomic changes from prior ileocolonic anastomosis. Mycophenolate mofetil was reduced to mitigate potential side effects, and loperamide was added for diarrhea control. His OxyContin dose was increased to manage worsening neck pain. He improved clinically, with kidney function returning to baseline, and was discharged home with services and follow-up plans.
